findings.explanation: There is repeated independent stereochemical re-derivation of the same answer by multiple agents after a verifier already checked the file. The Planner first lays out W1–W4 for Executor/Verifier in [M3], then later re-asks essentially the same descriptor check in [M13] after [M11] already verified D. Likewise, Executor repeats the full D analysis in [M7] after having produced a prior full derivation in [M2] and a conflicting B derivation in [M6], while Verifier independently re-derives the same final D assignment in [M11] after already doing so in [M5]. These are materially equivalent analysis/recheck efforts rather than new synthesis.

The handoff around the answer file is unstable: Executor’s switch to B in [M6] is not cleanly integrated with the rest of the team, and Verifier explicitly rejects it in [M8], noting the file holds B and instructing Executor to restore D. The subsequent correction is only partially coordinated until [M11] and [M12]; earlier, the request in [M4] to keep the file as D is contradicted by the later overwrite in [M6], showing a broken handoff/ownership flow. [M13] then has to restart the verification request because the prior check was tied to an outdated file state.

Relevant information was available but later ignored or contradicted without resolution. In [M5] and [M11], Verifier independently concludes D is correct, including the key regiochemistry (LDA gives the C6 enolate and Me ends up at C6). However, Executor later continues the conflicting B line in [M6], and Verifier in [M8] explicitly says D is the only option consistent with the stereo steps, rejecting B; the discussion then reopens the same issue in [M10]-[M13] even after the file is back to D. The most direct example of ignored information is Executor’s [M6] claim that B is best fit despite Verifier’s already-established D verdict in [M5].
